minutes.headline: School Committee heard a parent's account of a lost kindergartner on a bus and took up Bengals football field fees.
minutes.summary: The meeting opened with the new superintendent's report, including a kindergartner dismissal and bus-radio problem on the first day, then principals' back-to-school updates. The committee discussed the Bengals youth football turf-use agreement and bond payment, took public comment on the bus incident and a banquet exclusion, and approved a charge for a blizzard bag advisory committee. It went into executive session at the end.

public_comment.topic: Parent described her kindergartner going missing on the bus the first day, 50 minutes of panic, and asked for a written dismissal policy, more radios, bus stopping protocols and better ID tags.
Resident objected to being denied a seat at a booster banquet and asked to put booster-club event access on the next agenda.
Resident supported inviting all parents and friends to events, saying common sense should prevail.
Football program representatives urged cooperation on the Bengals bond payment and on concessions stand conditions.

votes.motion: Approve minutes of the August 15th regular session
Approve the charge for the alternative structured learning day advisory committee, with the addition of a school committee member
Enter executive session under MGL c30A s21 to conduct strategy sessions for contract negotiations with non-union personnel, not to return to public session

budget_items.what_was_said: A Bengals representative cited an amount outstanding on the bond and asked how to get past it.

budget_items.topic: Absorbing bond payment in school budget
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said the bond payment will be considered in next year's budget process so youth athletics may not have to pay a large amount.
A speaker suggested taking a small amount ten times to solve the bonding issue.
The principal is piloting a texting survey service for one month and would need PTO help to continue for the year.
The capital plan requests a substantial sum to continue asbestos abatement of spray-on material above ceilings.
A speaker asked that school, parks and town sit down to review fees for facility use before fiscal year 2020.
The district applied for a competitive literacy grant for primary school literacy instruction.

decisions.decision: The chair of the Board of Selectmen was contacted about a joint workshop on facility use and user fees.
Superintendent to communicate to building principals to gauge interest in staff, parent and student participation on the blizzard bag advisory committee.
Superintendent to return at the next meeting with the fall field/turf agreement with the Bengals.
Policy subcommittee to meet Monday at 6:30 and will look at the graduation requirements policy.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to approve the charge for a blizzard bag advisory committee, adding a School Committee member; the vote count was not audible.
The Bengals youth football turf agreement and bond payment ended with no resolution; the superintendent is to bring the fall field agreement to the next meeting.
The chair said the Bengals bond payment will be considered in next year's budget process, so youth athletics may not have to pay a large amount.
A parent told the committee her kindergartner went missing on a bus the first day and asked for a written dismissal policy, more radios and better ID tags.
A resident's objection to being denied a seat at a booster banquet was referred, with a request to put booster-club event access on a future agenda.

why_it_matters: Whether the school budget absorbs the football bond payment decides if the cost falls on youth athletics families or on the school budget, which is mostly paid by taxes.
The first-day bus incident raises questions about dismissal procedures and bus radios, which affect every family with young children riding the bus.

The policy subcommittee meeting Monday at 6:30, which will look at the graduation requirements policy.
